finding.title: A Partial module name that is a predefined macro is replaced before it names the file
finding.claim: Verdict: broken. In a GCC build the compiler predefines `unix` as 1. A test with `#include TEST_PARTIAL_PUBLIC_MODULE(unix)` and a `unix.c` module preprocesses to `#include "ceedling_partial_1_impl.h"`. Ceedling reads the directive as written and generates `ceedling_partial_unix_impl.{c,h}`. It also writes an empty `ceedling_partial_1_impl.h`. The test links without the module and fails with `undefined reference to 'unix_pub'`, under a notice that blames missing `#include` lines. `__PARTIALS_EXPAND(module)` expands the argument, and `_validate_module!` checks spelling only. This is the mechanism of #1460, which names the directory argument. The `_AT` module argument passes through `__PARTIALS_JOIN`, whose indirection also expands macros. That path was inferred and not built.

verifier.note: Core confirmed. (1) The notice blaming missing #include lines is not in captured evidence because run.sh's grep dropped it. (2) The #1460 reference cannot be checked against the repo.

finding.title: test:path matches a substring of the test's directory, not of its whole path
finding.claim: Verdict: partly kept. The docs say "tests whose path contains the given string". The code tests `File.dirname(test).include?(arg)` on the project-relative test path, with `\` turned into `/`. With tests in `test/unit`, `test/unit_extra` and `test/integration`: `test:path[unit]` ran 2 tests (substring, so `unit_extra` too), `test:path[nit]` ran 2, `test:path[t/in]` ran 1, `test:path[unit/]` found none (no trailing separator in a dirname), `test:path[test_foo.c]` found none (filename excluded) and `test:path[Test]` found none (case).

verifier.note: test:path[Test] found none (case) was never run in run_cli.sh/results.txt; it follows from the code.

finding.title: test:pattern matches a regular expression against the project-relative test path
finding.claim: Verdict: kept. The code applies `test =~ /#{regex}/` to each collected test path. Collected paths are relative to the project, so `^test/unit/` matched one test and the absolute directory of the project is never part of the text (`test:path[gap-10]` found nothing).

verifier.note: test:path[gap-10] found nothing was not in run_cli.sh; inferred from code and relative paths.

finding.title: Dependency fetch runs in the fetch path and build steps run in the source path
finding.claim: Verdict: kept. Fetch steps run inside `spec.fetch_path` after it is created, so a relative archive `:source` is relative to the fetch path. Each build step runs in `spec.source_path`, and the source, build and artifact paths are created first. Both use `WorkingDir.chdir`.

verifier.note: Core right. 'Each build step runs in spec.source_path' holds only for command-line steps; a :build_lib Symbol step goes to build_builtin without a chdir (line 218). Path creation (line 214) happens only when build steps exist (lines 209-212 return first).

finding.title: A mixin simple name is told from a filepath by extension or the forward slash only
finding.claim: Verdict: untestable here (Windows). `PathValidator#filepath?` returns true for a value with an extension or one containing `File::SEPARATOR`, which is `/` on every platform. The docs say "no path separator" and the project docs accept `\`. Whether a Windows `--mixin bar\base` (no extension) reaches this test unstandardized was not traced.

verifier.note: Verifier returned confirmed on the code description but found the Windows worry unfounded: command line, environment and :enabled mixin values are run through standardize_paths, which turns \ into /, before filepath? sees them (cli_handler.rb:49,587,611-617; mixinator.rb:85; mixin_resolvinator.rb:89). Recorded as partly by the investigator because the 'untestable' verdict and the hedge in the claim are wrong.

finding.title: Which Ceedling picks WHICH_CEEDLING, then :which_ceedling, then vendor/ceedling, then the gem, with ~ expanded
finding.claim: Verdict: kept. `InstallationSelector#select` takes the first of the environment variable, the config value and `vendor/ceedling` and falls back to the launcher's own root. `validate` standardizes the value, which expands `~`. Every experiment log here shows `Launching Ceedling from /home/user/Ceedling/` from `:which_ceedling`.

verifier.note: Code claim right. 'Every experiment log here shows Launching Ceedling from :which_ceedling' is overstated: the launch line names no source, and only release logs show 'Set which Ceedling from config'. No experiment exercises ~ expansion.

finding.title: Unity runner :includes entries are written to the runner as typed
finding.claim: Verdict: kept. With `:test_runner` ↳ `:includes: [foo.h, sub/missing.h]` the runner holds `#include "foo.h"` and `#include "sub/missing.h"`, and the compiler finds both through the `:include` path.

verifier.note: Behaviour holds. Cited evidence file results_include_min.txt does not hold the runner head, and no script creates project.runner.yml or include/sub/missing.h.

finding.title: The ${5} search path list holds more than the :paths and path-macro entries the tools doc names
finding.claim: Verdict: partly kept. The doc says `-I"${5}"` expands to the search paths of `:paths` plus build directive path macros. The real test compile line puts the test's mocks root, Partials roots and each Partial subdirectory first, then `:include` entries, then the vendor roots. `:paths` ↳ `:test` and ↳ `:source` directories are not on it.

verifier.note: Core right. ':paths :test and :source directories are not on it' holds only when the test directory has no header; a :test directory holding a header is added. Real list also holds TEST_INCLUDE_PATH, :support, :libraries and test-toolchain include entries.

finding.title: The tools doc's compile and link examples show a layout Ceedling does not build
finding.claim: Verdict: broken (illustrative). The example compile line has `-I"project/tests" -I"project/source"` and outputs `build/tests/out/source.o`. The linker example writes `build\tests\out\test_thing.exe`. Ceedling builds objects at `build/test/out/<test path>/_t_/<mirrored source path>.o`. Source and test directories are not `-I` entries.

verifier.note: Output paths right (build/test/out/<test>/_t_/ not build/tests/out). 'Test directories are not -I entries' is overstated: a :test directory holding headers is on -I.

finding.title: Cppcheck suppression files come from :paths :cppcheck and :files :cppcheck
finding.claim: Verdict: kept. Each `:paths` ↳ `:cppcheck` entry contributes its `*.xml` and `*<extension>` files, a path that does not exist logs a warning, and `:files` ↳ `:cppcheck` revises the list. `files:cppcheck` lists the result.

verifier.note: Core right. 'A path that does not exist logs a warning' is wrong as a general statement: collect_paths drops a plain nonexistent entry before collect_suppressions sees it. The warning can fire only for a nonexistent entry ending in /** or /*, where with_parents re-adds the base.
